!`git status --short 2>/dev/null | head -40`
!`git diff --stat HEAD 2>/dev/null | tail -40`

**Target:** `$ARGUMENTS` (empty → the working tree). One high-recall pass on Fable, in a forked context: you see only this skill and the target — resolve everything from the repo, and make your **final message the Output section verbatim**, nothing else, so the caller receives the findings intact. Surface **every real issue**; confidence decides a finding's tier, never whether it's reported. **Output:** one ranked findings list. This is the only review entry point — never a hand-spawned `changes-review` agent. **Each file is read once and reviewed once** — no re-sweeps. One pass per change set: a workflow never re-runs this skill on its own fix commits.

## 1 — Resolve the range

| Args | Diff |
|------|------|
| none | `git diff HEAD` + untracked files |
| paths | `git diff HEAD -- <paths>` |
| a branch | `git fetch` if remote, then `git diff <base>...<head>` |
| `<base>...<head>` | `git diff <base>...<head>` |
| PR number | `gh pr view <n>`, `gh pr diff <n>` |
| `plan=<path>` (extra token) | read that plan for intent and the `Trivial:` claims |

Default base `main` (else `master`, else the default branch). Always three-dot. **Read-only** — fetch only; read head-ref files with `git show <head>:<path>`; never checkout, pull, commit, reset, or stash.

## 2 — Intent and surface

Read the goal (PR description / commit messages / plan) so deliberate choices aren't flagged, and apply the lineage test (a recorded *Fix on sight* change passes it, `development-practices.md`). List every changed file and symbol — your coverage checklist. Read each changed file in full at the head ref — except generated files (a `Code generated … DO NOT EDIT.` header or the project's generated paths): review their source (proto, schema, template, `wire.go`) instead, and flag a generated file changed without its source as hand-edited (`must_fix`). Read the changed symbols' callers (`codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_impact`) — bugs live in unchanged callers too. If a trigger in `~/.claude/templates/cross-cutting.md` applies, walk its layers against the diff and the repo's `.claude/rules/cross-cutting.md` — **the defect is usually in a file the diff did not touch**, so search for what should have changed with it.

## 3 — Review each file once, against every lens

- **Correctness:**
  - edge cases (empty/zero/boundaries/unicode/large/first-run)
  - error paths (unchecked returns, swallowed exceptions, partial failure without rollback)
  - concurrency and shared state
  - resource lifecycle (leaks, cleanup skipped on early return)
  - contracts (changed signatures with stale callers, breaking persisted/wire formats, migration order)
  - cross-cutting (`cross-cutting.md`: a layer the change reaches but did not update — a new cloud/queue/storage call without its permission grant in the same change, a new deployable without its image repository or CI path, a CI workflow missing a token permission, a config field missing from an environment, a renamed metric with a stale dashboard or alert, a new query without tenant scoping; two files that must agree — source and generated output, a lock file, an image pinned per environment — neither generated nor guarded; a trigger with no Cross-cutting lines)
  - rollout (code that needs infrastructure or a migration not yet live at deploy, old and new versions unable to coexist during the rollout, a manual step a merge will not perform left unstated, no rollback path, an irreversible step not called out)
- **Quality:**
  - security (injection, authn/z, secrets, unvalidated boundary input, SSRF/path traversal)
  - performance (uncached hot paths, N+1, redundant work)
  - dead code (confirm "unused" with a caller search)
  - consistency and DRY (MUST cite the existing pattern/implementation `file:line`; when a plan is given, new code matches each Gold Standards entry's Copy items or records a Deviation)
  - tests (`testing.md`: behavior assertions a one-character bug would fail, tier-correct doubles — a violation is `must_fix` — parsimony, new deps mocked in all existing tests)
  - standards (file > 800 excluding generated files, function > 50, nesting > 4, untyped `any`, bare `except:`, hardcoded config)
  - design (`code-addition-checklist.md`: the One Idea — a concrete type where a core interface belongs, impl selection by `if`/import instead of a `Kind` factory, a factory with no stub default or a silent fallback on an unknown kind, construction or I/O outside the composition root, globals/singletons, coupling, leaking layers)
  - codegen (hand-written code a project generator should own, a hand-edited generated file, a source change without regenerated output, a repeated shape that should be a template)
  - config (env read outside the config layer, a field with no fail-safe `base` default or no doc, a hard-coded value that belongs in config)
  - resilience (an external call without a timeout, retry/breaker/logging inlined instead of a decorator, retry on a permanent error, a doubled-up retry over an SDK that already retries)
  - errors (code-less errors, internal detail leaked past the transport edge)
  - observability (silent failure branches, context-free errors, a new path with no log/metric/span, missing trace correlation)
  - docs — `must_fix` (`documentation-sync.md`): a changed symbol whose doc comment wasn't revised, an inline comment or docstring — in the diff or on a caller you read — that contradicts the code, a test without its Why/What doc, a README / docs page / CLAUDE.md / ADR / generated reference that now describes old behavior, a missing doc for a new symbol, flag, config field or endpoint, a `Docs-Impact: none` claim the diff contradicts
  - suppressions (a new `nolint`/`noqa`/`type: ignore`/`eslint-disable`/`ts-ignore`, exemption or baseline entry, raised ratchet ceiling, or skipped/xfailed test the user didn't approve — `must_fix`: revert it and fix the code)
  - bloat (`code-addition-checklist.md` *Budget*: an interface/`Kind`/factory/config field for an internal collaborator with one implementation, hand-written ceremony a generator could emit, a test re-asserting a lower tier's behavior or testing structure, a CLI step wrapping a stock tool, a generic capability built in the product instead of the shared library — name the lines that can go)
- **Tests changed?** Read `~/.claude/rules/testing-authoring.md` first (it loads only when *editing* tests) and the project's `.claude/rules/testing-project.md` if present.

File anything that *might* be an issue — "not sure" means `suggestion`, not silence. Before keeping a `must_fix`, try to refute it against the code; keep it only if it survives.

## 4 — Close out

One line per zero-finding file saying why it's clean — you can't write the line without having reviewed it. No second sweep.

## `deep` (opt-in, costly)

Only when args include `deep`: also run `Skill(skill='code-review', args='max <target>')` (a multi-agent adversarial pass; never `--fix`) and fold its findings in unculled. It runs in the background — never write the output without its findings, never fabricate them.

## Output

One list, most severe first, exact duplicates dropped; every finding has `file:line`; `must_fix` / `should_fix` carry a concrete failure scenario.

```
## Findings
### must_fix — breaks correctness or security
- [file:line] Issue — failure scenario (inputs/state → wrong result)
### should_fix — maintainability, coverage, convention, documented standards
- [file:line] Issue — why
### suggestion — optional, or real but lower-confidence
- [file:line] Improvement
## Human review — read in full; the rest is sampled
- [file] auth / permissions / migration / public contract / infrastructure / first instance of a new pattern
```

Say so when a tier is empty. The caller decides what happens next: `spec-verify` turns every tier into one fix commit; a user who typed `/review-diff` is asked which findings to address.
